papers.title: Visitor's note
lines: On the shortest day the sun shines down the passage and lights the chamber for a few minutes.
Five thousand years ago someone planned that. I stood in the dark and held my breath.

trail.clue: A visitor left a keepsake near the standing stone. 'Where the sun finds the door.'

papers.title: Archaeologist's note
lines: Dated the passage tomb at about 3200 BC. Older than the Pyramids, older than Stonehenge.
The builders left no writing and rather a lot of spirals. We are working on it.

papers.title: Battle brochure
lines: The Battle of the Boyne, 1690. Two kings, two armies, one river, a great deal of paperwork.
The battle was a day. The arguments about it have gone on rather longer.

papers.title: Farmer's field note
lines: The Hill of Tara is where the High Kings were crowned, say the books.
My cows graze on it. They do not mind. They have also been crowned, in a manner of speaking, with daisies.
